rules.name: School Requirements (Engineering Breadth):
rules.desc: School of Engineering (SoE) requires SoE Breadth to be fulfilled. These are a set of defined subjects that provide you with a well-rounded education in the Engineering field. You will gain a foundation in critical topics for being an engineer. You should pay close attention to the notes in each section as certain classes and stipulations are required depending on the Methods Depth Track you pursue.

children.name: Mathematics
children.desc: Mathematics consists of the single-variable, or multi-variable, calculus series along with statistics courses.
children.notes:
A) 20 units minimum required for the (Physical Methods Track) and (AI Methods Track).
B) 15 units minimum required for the (Human Behavior Methods Track).
C) (MATH 19), (MATH 20), and 6 units of Mathematics can be waived only if you receive a grade of C or better in (Math 21). The course waiver automatically is made on a student’s My Academic Path (MAP) page, but you must ask the Design Student Services Officer to manually waive the associated units in the Mathematics section.
D) (MATH 21) needs to be taken either at Stanford or with the equivalent transfer work. Students can replace the (MATH 21) requirement if they take a class that makes substantial use of the concepts in (MATH 21) while also receiving a grade of C or better: (MATH 53), (MATH 106), (MATH 115), or (CME 102).
E) A score of 5 on the (AP Calculus BC test) is equivalent to (MATH 19), (MATH 20), (MATH 21) and gives students 10 units towards Mathematics.
F) A score of 4 on (AP Calculus BC test) or 5 on the (AP Calculus AB test) is equivalent to only (MATH 19) and (MATH 20) and gives students only 6 units towards Mathematics. The AP substitution, and units, is made automatically on a student’s My Academic Path (MAP) page.
G) (MATH 51) or (CME 100) is only required for the (Physical Methods Track) or (AI Methods Track). (CS 103) is also a suitable option for (AI Methods Track).

children.name: Behavioral Science
children.desc: Behavioral Sciences draws on the social sciences to study human behavior.
children.notes: A) No other (PSYCH) or (PSYC) class is allowed.

children.name: Additional School of Engineering Math and Science (Additional SoE Math & Science):
children.desc: Additional SoE Math and Science is where allowed classes posted by SoE for Mathematics and Science may be applied. The number of courses for use here may vary based on the remaining units you need to reach the 30 unit required minimum.
children.notes:
A) Design abides by the Allowed List of Mathematics Courses and the Allowed List of Science Courses from School of Engineering.
B) Quantity of courses varies based on the units needed to reach 30 units.
C) (PHYSICS 41) is required for (Physical Methods Track). Students may choose (PHYSICS 41) or (PHYSICS 41E), but both cannot be taken towards the major.
D) (CS 103) and (CS 109) are recommended for (AI Methods Track).
E) If (MATH 51) and (CME 100) are both taken, only 8 units of credit will be allowed towards the Design major due to overlapping material.
F) More advanced Mathematics or Statistics courses may be considered through petition.
G) ACE courses are encouraged for students that seek additional support with MATH or CS courses, but the ACE credit may not count towards the major unit minimum requirements.

children.name: Technology in Society (TiS)
children.desc: Technology in Society is devoted to exploring ethical, social issues, and responsibilities arising from the interplay of engineering, technology, and society. You must take one course.
children.notes:
A) Design abides by the Allowed List of Technology in Society courses from School of Engineering.
B) (ENERGY 177A) and (ENERGY 177B) must both be taken, and for 3 units each, to fulfill TiS.
C) (NBIO 101) is by application, and must be taken for 3 units and a letter grade to fulfill TiS.

children.name: Engineering Fundamentals
children.desc: Engineering Fundamentals is a set of technically rigorous introductory courses chosen from the various engineering disciplines. They provide knowledge about major fields, they give an opportunity to explore a number of engineering topics before embarking on a specific engineering major, and each class offers a reasonable insight into a contemporary technological subject for the interested non-engineer. You must complete a minimum of two Engineering Fundamentals courses.
children.notes:
A) Design abides by the Allowed List of Engineering Fundamental courses from School of Engineering.
B) (ENGR 14) is required for (Physical Methods Track).
C) (CS 106A) is required for (AI Methods Track).
D) Only (CS 106A) or (CS 106B) counts towards Engineering Fundamentals.
E) (CS 106M) is a companion course to (CS 106B), for 1 unit, but may not count as a standalone course fulfilling Engineering Fundamentals.

rules.name: Design Core
rules.desc: The Design Core are signature courses to our major program. It consists of defined classes where you will learn, work, collaborate, and cultivate skills among your design peers. Each course has its own learning outcomes and priorities. It is an integrated sequence that delves into topics of needfinding, user research, expressing ideas visually, rapid prototyping across media, building to think business factors, and storytelling (among other subjects). A key component to all our core classes is the ethics and implications of producing design work.
rules.notes:
• (DESIGN 1) and (Design 11) have limited space which may impact the quarter you enroll.

• (DESIGN 121) should be completed spring of sophomore year, or fall of junior year.

• (DESIGN 160R) should be taken junior year.

• (DESIGN 151) is strongly recommended for students following a 2025-2026 Program Sheet or a 2026-2027 Program Sheet.

rules.name: Methods Depth Areas
rules.desc:
Methods lets you take classes across the university to sharpen making skills, abilities, and gain professional fluency.
You will choose one of three Method Depths tracks listed below:
[1] Physical Design + Manufacturing — Methods range from classes on materials and mechanisms (to understand what is possible with physical design) to manufacturing processes and supply chain logistics (to understand how physical design is implemented).
[2] AI + Digital User Experience — Methods range from foundational programming methodologies and human-computer interaction classes to applied courses on digital prototyping, user experience design, and incorporating AI and data science.
[3] Human Behavior + Multi-stakeholder Research — Methods span qualitative and quantitative approaches to better understand people – who we are, what we do, and why we do it. Classes focus on communication, data science, and psychology to help understand how to design for the human experience.
rules.notes: To fulfill a Methods Depth, you will take four classes focused on foundational understanding and application.

children.name: Physical Design + Manufacturing
children.notes:
A) Prerequisites: The following may be prerequisites for these Method classes. All are also expected to be taken in the SoE Mathematics, Science, and Engineering Fundamentals categories for (Physical Design + Manufacturing Methods Track):
Engineering Fundamentals - (ENGR 14)

Math - (CME 100) / (Math 51)

Science - (PHYSICS 41)

children.name: AI + Digital User Experience
children.notes:
A) Prerequisites: The following may be prerequisites for these Method classes. All are also expected to be taken in the SoE Mathematics, Science, and Engineering Fundamentals categories for the (Physical Design + Manufacturing Methods Track). They may include others (please consult course-specific prerequisites):
Engineering Fundamentals - (CS 106A)

Math - (Math 51) / (CME 100)
(CS 103, CS 109 recommended)

children.name: Human Behavior + Multi-stakeholder Research
children.notes: A) (HUMBIO 82A) prepares students for advanced research work (ie, for an honors thesis), and students should be planning to do subsequent research work beyond the class.

rules.name: Domain Focus Areas
rules.desc:
A Domain Focus Area is a unique opportunity for you to immerse in a field that you are curious about or motivated by. You can apply your design abilities within a specific context, and emerge having a changed perspective. Each of the domain sphere options is saturated with wicked problems where design work is useful and needed.
You will choose one of four Domain Focus Areas listed below:
[1] Designing for the Planet — A domain sphere including Climate, Environment, Oceans, and Energy (and more). Gain knowledge around environmental problem solving at macro and micro scales, on all corners of our planet.
[2] Designing for Biological Futures — A domain sphere including Living Matter and Synthetic Biology (and more). Learn about biofutures and explore the possibilities of building with biology.
[3] Designing for Health — A domain sphere including Healthcare & Health Technology Innovation (and more). Investigate domestic and global governance and their intersection with development, economics, and a more equitable society.
[4] Designing for Social Impact — A domain sphere including Global Development, Social Systems, Social Inequity (and more). Gain understanding in anatomy, physiology, healthcare systems, and health technology while exploring a new era of personalized, accessible, and patient-centered care.
rules.notes:
To fulfill a Domain, you will pursue a three-course “pathway”. Students take 3 classes total: one or more class from [List A], and the remaining classes from [List B]. You should plan your Domain classes and work with the guidance of a d.school Domain Co-Lead. Chosen domains and associated courses must be on the approved list in the year taken.
Note: Domain requirements updated to the [List A] and [List B] format beginning in 2025-2026. If you are following an earlier program sheet from 2023-2024 or 2024-2025, you will follow the 2024-2025 Domain list of classes that utilizes the [Foundational], [Applied], and [Future Horizons] categories.

rules.name: Capstone Courses
rules.desc: For your Capstone, you will scope and execute design work that integrates and draws upon what you have learned across your engineering breadth, design core, methods depth and your domain focus area. You will choose from two available Capstone sequences.
